card.name: Kizomba
card.tagline: Angola's slow, sensual partner dance born of semba and zouk
card.profile: Kizomba is a social dance and music genre that originated in Luanda, Angola, in the late 1970s to early 1980s, emerging as a fusion of Angolan semba with Antillean zouk, slowing the cadence and adding a stronger bass line (Wikipedia). The word means "party" in Kimbundu. As a dance it is a close-embrace couple dance in which the leader guides with torso and right arm, aiming for smooth, synchronized footwork expressed through the attitude called ginga (women) and banga (men); it is traditionally danced at parties and weddings.
card.insight: Eduardo Paim — with his band SOS and the album "Luanda, Minha Banda" (1992) — is, per the Embassy of Angola, "often referred to as the 'father of kizomba'"; the genre spread globally via the Lusophone diaspora and was declared a National Intangible Cultural Heritage by Angola's Ministry of Culture on April 18, 2024.

lessons.teacher_style: The teacher provides clear, step-by-step instructions with a focus on body mechanics and posture. She uses simple, relatable analogies to help students understand the nuances of the dance.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teacher emphasizes the importance of keeping the energy down and avoiding any tapping, which is a common feature in other dance styles.
what_hinders: the teacher's fast pace in some segments
